bottom_line: In EMPEROR-Preserved, empagliflozin vs placebo reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.90).
implications: These data support that empagliflozin, compared with placebo, reduced the composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure (0.79; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.90) and reduced hospitalizations for heart failure (e.g., hospitalization for heart failure hazard ratio, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.60 to 0.83). They do not show a clear reduction in cardiovascular death (hazard ratio, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.76 to 1.09) or death from any cause (hazard ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.15).

major_points.text: Double-blind randomized trial comparing empagliflozin 10 mg once daily vs placebo on top of usual therapy in HF with EF >40%.
major_points.quote: In this double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 5988 patients with class II–IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of more than 40% to receive empagliflozin (10 mg once daily) or placebo, in addition to usual therapy.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was time to first event of a composite of adjudicated cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure.

major_points.text: Primary outcome occurred less often with empagliflozin than placebo over a median 26.2 months (HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.69–0.90; P<0.001).
major_points.quote: Over a median of 26.2 months, a primary outcome event occurred in 415 of 2997 patients (13.8%) in the empagliflozin group and in 511 of 2991 patients (17.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.69 to 0.90; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Effect on the primary outcome was mainly related to lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure; CV death component was not clearly reduced.
major_points.quote: This effect was mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure in the empagliflozin group.

major_points.text: Total (first and recurrent) hospitalizations for heart failure were lower with empagliflozin (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.61–0.88; P<0.001).
major_points.quote: The total number of hospitalizations for heart failure was lower in the empagliflozin group than in the placebo group (407 with empagliflozin and 541 with placebo; hazard ratio, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.61 to 0.88; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Certain adverse events were more frequent with empagliflozin, including uncomplicated genital and urinary tract infections and hypotension.
major_points.quote: Uncomplicated genital and urinary tract infections and hypotension were reported more frequently with empagliflozin.

criticisms.text: Between-group differences for hazard ratios or treatment differences outside the testing hierarchy were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; intervals should not be used to infer definitive treatment effects.
criticisms.quote: For all hazard ratios or treatment differences not included in the testing hierarchy, no adjustment has been made for multiple comparisons, so the intervals should not be used to infer definitive treatment effects.
